clue.text: Fashion follows like goods from capital in the sun

indicators.note: follows puts the fashion word after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: akin, of like kind, so like gives kin
GS, G for good doubled into a plural, stands for goods
ton is an old word for high fashion, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: Stylish wares travel out from a sunny capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria's 'goods' as GS is loose; the capital meant is Kingston, Jamaica, a famously sunny Caribbean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingston is the capital city of Jamaica, a sunshine island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Spirit after 4 for sucker

definitions.meaning: whisky distilled in Scotland is a spirit
placed after 4 (BUTTER) it makes a boiled sweet one sucks

explanation.definitionFit: Scotch whisky is a spirit, and the word ends the name of a hard toffee for sucking.

clue.text: Architect's friend, child to 10

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a lad is a male child
the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: An architect's friend sends a child off to number 10.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but is simply read as the letters I O. The 's after Architect is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Palladio was the Renaissance Italian architect whose villas inspired Palladian style.

clue.text: Fat hatter's stopwatch?

definitions.meaning: a dairy fat spread on bread
in Alice in Wonderland the Mad Hatter's watch stopped after it was greased with 'the best' of this

explanation.definitionFit: Butter is an animal fat, and Carroll's Hatter spread it in his watch works until the watch stopped.

clue.text: Student embraced by bird needs shrink

indicators.note: embraced by puts the student letter inside the bird

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A learner hugged by a songbird needs a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like the slang noun for a psychiatrist; it is the verb, to recoil.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to recoil or draw back, which is to shrink from something.

clue.text: One of 4's followers that can't hold a measure of liquor

definitions.text: One of 4's followers that can't hold
definitions.meaning: after BUTTER it makes the hands of someone who keeps dropping things
a depth of spirit in a glass as wide as a digit

explanation.definitionFit: A finger is both a digit (butter-fingered hands drop things) and a small measure of spirit poured into a glass.

clue.text: Overbid ends in grasp of Forrest

indicators.note: in grasp of puts the ends inside the film character's surname

parts.note: Forrest Gump is the title character of the 1994 film
A and Z are the two ends of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone overbids at the extremes of Forrest's reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' are not the ends of a word but the alphabet's, A to Z. GAZUMP is British property slang for a seller taking a higher offer after agreeing a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazump is to outbid a buyer who had agreed a house price, so to overbid.

clue.text: Fear of fairy in Italian girl

indicators.note: in puts the fairy inside the girl's name

parts.note: Pia is an Italian girl's name
a hob is a hobgoblin or household fairy

explanation.surface: Fear of a fairy lurks within an Italian girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an irrational fear or dread of something.

clue.text: Scope increased to form circle with directions

parts.note: compass means range or scope
rose means went up, increased

explanation.surface: A telescope's range was enlarged to make a ring showing the points.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass rose is the circular figure on maps and charts marking north, south, east and west.

clue.text: Man with title that can't go straight

definitions.meaning: a man dubbed Sir by the monarch
the chess piece moves in an L-shape, never in a straight line

explanation.definitionFit: A knight holds the title Sir, and the chess knight jumps in an L rather than straight lines.

clue.text: Offering to drop one thousand pounds from debt

indicators.note: to drop means the following letters are taken out of the debt word

parts.note: an obligation is a debt owed
I is the Roman numeral one
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An offer to write off a thousand-pound debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a religious offering, especially bread and wine presented to God.

clue.text: 4 won't if one's very proper, suffering hit on emoluments

indicators.note: suffering signals these words being knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A prim person sees no butter melt while their salary takes a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the saying 'butter wouldn't melt in one's mouth', said of someone who looks very prim and proper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says butter would not soften on the tongue of an apparently demure person.

clue.text: Way to do my cipher which gets under one's skin

indicators.note: Way to suggests a method of treating these letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A method for cracking my cipher that really irritates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets under one's skin' wants to mean annoys; read literally it is the needle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic syringe injects beneath the skin, so it literally penetrates a person's flesh.

clue.text: See 11
In Rome almost nothing happens without some escort being unaware

indicators.note: without means outside, so the Italian word goes round the other piece
almost means the last letter of the Italian word is dropped

parts.note: in Rome, i.e. in Italian, nothing is niente

indicators.note: some means only part of the word escort is taken

explanation.surface: In Rome nearly nothing occurs without some escort, so one stays ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' says the word for nothing is Italian, and 'almost' drops its last letter. 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescient is a learned word for ignorant, lacking knowledge, from Latin nescire.

clue.text: Managed entry into what's available, being broad-minded

indicators.note: entry into puts the managed word inside the phrase for a vacant property

parts.note: to let is the sign on a property available to rent
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone who managed to get into a rental is open-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: TO LET is the British sign on a house or flat available to rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerant person accepts other views and ways, which is being broad-minded.

clue.text: Ship holding catch is a cutter

indicators.note: holding means the ship letters go round the catch word

parts.note: SS is steamship
to catch a remark is to hear it

explanation.surface: A vessel carrying the haul is a fast boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a sailing vessel, matching 'Ship', but it is the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears are a large cutting tool like scissors, used for gardens or sheep.

clue.text: Backward setter has stratagem to use

indicators.note: Backward means the setter's pronoun is read from right to left

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
a ploy is a stratagem or ruse

explanation.surface: A setter who is behind the times has a clever trick to deploy.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to put it to use.

clue.text: I'm not sure young scientist should be in cast — it's torture

indicators.note: should be in puts the doubt and graduate inside the cast word

parts.note: threw means cast, as in cast a stone
um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure
a BSc, Bachelor of Science, is a newly qualified scientist

explanation.surface: A hesitant young researcher should join the cast, and it's agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbscrews were an instrument of torture crushing the thumbs, so the word stands for that torment.

clue.text: Fabric for 4 once, very nearly religious one

indicators.note: very nearly means the word is one letter short of right, its last letter changed

parts.note: a Muslim is a follower of Islam

explanation.surface: A cloth used to wrap butter in the old days is almost a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria's loose wordplay: MUSLIM with one letter wrong. 'Butter muslin' is a fine cotton once used to wrap butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslin is a fine cotton cloth, and butter muslin was used for straining and wrapping dairy products.

clue.text: Shielded monster with nervy disposition

indicators.note: disposition, an arranging, signals rearranging the letters of nervy

explanation.surface: A guarded beast with a jittery temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, but means arrangement, rearranging NERVY into YVERN. 'Shielded' means borne on a heraldic shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a two-legged winged dragon used as a charge in heraldry.

clue.text: Little 4 in way to fulfil ambition

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words fulfil ambition

explanation.surface: Some small butter on the road to achieving a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Here a 'butter' is something that butts, like a ram, so a little one is its young.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep is little, and grows into a ram, an animal that butts.

clue.text: Cycle rides with charge rebutted that sweet talk won't 4

indicators.note: rebutted, pushed back, signals both pieces read backwards together

parts.note: spins are short rides, e.g. on a bicycle
a rap is a criminal charge

explanation.surface: Cycling trips accompanied by a rebutted charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'fine words butter no parsnips': flattery achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says fine words butter no parsnips, so flattery cannot coat these root vegetables.

clue.text: Right one in base is masculine

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the base word

parts.note: base means low, vile
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The right one in a base is a manly type.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means having manly strength and vigour.

clue.text: Tavern in heaven not serving stout?

indicators.note: in puts the tavern inside the heavens word

parts.note: the sky, poetically the heavens
an inn is a tavern

explanation.surface: A pub in paradise that doesn't serve stout beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the dark beer, fitting the tavern, but it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny means very thin, so the reverse of stout or plump.

clue.text: Spirit before 4 for Christmas pudding

definitions.meaning: set before 4 (BUTTER) it names the sweet sauce served with Christmas pudding

explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a distilled spirit, and brandy butter is the rich sauce eaten with Christmas pudding.
